title: envelope
description: Wrapper carried by every event regardless of type. The envelope is how the substrate navigates the log without understanding any payload. `v` versions the envelope; `type_v` versions the payload. The two change independently.

v.description: Envelope version. The one field whose name and position never change: readers check it first, and refuse a version they do not know rather than guess. Bump only for a breaking envelope change; adding an optional envelope field does not bump.

id.description: ULID. The event's identity. Never reuse. Not the cursor: concurrent writers can commit ULIDs out of order, so the store's commit sequence is the cursor.

ts.description: RFC3339 UTC, millisecond precision. Redundant with the ULID prefix but kept because humans and SQL both want a real timestamp.

type.description: Event type, e.g. 'candidate.measured'. Everything dispatches on this string. Every type has a schema in schema/<type>/; append rejects a type with no schema and a payload that does not match.

type_v.description: Payload version for THIS type only, independent of `v` and of every other type. Resolve against schema/<type>/v<type_v>.json to interpret the payload. Readers that encounter an unknown version should refuse rather than guess.

subject.description: What this event is ABOUT (not who wrote it — that is `actor`), as 'prefix:rest'. Known prefixes: prog:sha256:<hex>, bench:<name>, pool:<name>, schema:<type>. New prefixes may be added; the 'prefix:rest' shape is the contract. Supplied by the writer; each type's schema description says which subject to use. history(subject) retrieves everything about one thing, across all actors.

actor.description: Provenance: who produced this event. Required as a key, but its CONTENTS are free — add fields whenever a new loop architecture needs them. This is what later answers 'did Opus-authored programs outperform Qwen mutations, per token spent?'

role.description: Free string naming the position in whatever architecture is current, e.g. 'researcher', 'lab_assistant', 'verifier', 'human'. Deliberately not an enum: a future loop that isn't researcher/assistant shaped must not require a schema change.

model.description: Model identifier, or absent for pure-code actors. e.g. 'claude-opus-5', 'qwen3.8-flash-next-fp4'.

harness.description: Which loop generation wrote this, ideally path@git-sha, e.g. 'loops/v1@a3f9c21'. Lets you segment results by the code that produced them after a rewrite.

cause.description: WHY THIS EVENT EXISTS: id of the event that prompted it, or null. A program.committed points at the direction or human instruction that asked for it; a candidate.measured at the program.committed it scored; a decision.made at the direction it answers. Follow it to attribute results to the idea that caused them — this is what answers whether the expensive model is earning its budget. Do not confuse with a program's `parent` (what code it came from).

payload.description: Type-specific body, validated on write against schema/<type>/v<type_v>.json.
